Rainbow Loom® DUO Combo with JEWEL Rubber Bands Collection, Features 2 connectable Rainbow Looms to make LONGER and WIDER creations, an Organizer Case, Great activity up to 4 people 7+ The actual Rainbow Looms are the real star of this kit. So many refill kits only include 2-prong or Y-looms, even refill kits from Rainbow Loom. They call their 2-prong looms Happy Looms, and this kit does have two of those, plus the two big teal Rainbow Looms. The Rainbow Looms can be connected to each other, so that you can have a very long loom or a very wide loom.

The kit includes some instructions, but they aren’t the clearest. Videos are the place to learn the coolest techniques. I started making bracelets to keep my hands busy, and learned so much from YouTube.

In my opinion, the band colors are subpar. They are supposed to be from the JEWEL collection: green, purple, gold, black, white, baby pink, pink, blue, teal, and yellow. The white bands are actually clear. The baby pink bands are so pale they’re nearly clear too. The yellow bands are more like a yellow glow-in-the-dark, very very light yellow. The teal bands are flat teal, they don’t have any pearly or translucent sheen.

The storage box is nice, it has compartments for everything, including the pony beads and C-Clips. There are even slots for the crochet hooks. The box latches shut, so if the box gets knocked over, you shouldn’t have a mess to clean up. But the box is delicate -- mine arrived with several cracks in it, and a piece broken off the lid. So that’s something to be aware of if you take the box on the go.
text_fidelity_b: Rainbow Loom® DUO Combo with JEWEL Rubber Bands Collection, Features 2 connectable Rainbow Looms to make LONGER and WIDER creations, an Organizer Case, Great activity up to 4 people 7+

text_fidelity_a:
rudy games - Lost Galaxy 2019 - The Intergalactic Card Game - Interactive Game for Children 8 Years and Up and Adults We've been doing family game nights since I was a kid. So for my 70th birthday, pizza and a game were an obvious choice. Two of my sisters, a nephew, and I played Lost Galaxy for the first time and except for the fact that the birthday boy came in third place we had a great time doing it.

The instructions say you don't need any instructions, just download the app and get started. We did that and the first round of three was a bit of a mess. We had to stop the app frequently, going back and forth, checking the help tab and so on trying to understand what we were doing. That didn't take too long though. By the second round people were catching on nicely and the game started getting competitive as folks began developing some strategy. By the third round, the game play was positively cutthroat, with one sibling loudly announcing "No more Ms Nice Sister!" The poor birthday boy - me - lost several turns due to enemy action and to cosmic upheavals, which every one else greatly enjoyed. I greatly enjoyed all the moaning and groaning I got to do. 🙂

The age range at the table was 13, 54, 60, and 70 with everyone unanimously agreeing that this was a great game that would immediately join our stash of family games. It was a sweet way to celebrate turning 70 and Lost Galaxy will always be a part of my memories of that night.
text_fidelity_b: rudy games - Lost Galaxy 2019 - The Intergalactic Card Game - Interactive Game for Children 8 Years and Up and Adults

LEGO Disney Frozen Elsa's Magical Ice Palace 43172 Toy Castle Building Kit with Mini Dolls, Castle Playset with Popular Frozen Characters Including Elsa, Olaf, Anna and More (701 Pieces) This LEGO DISNEY PRINCESS ELSA’S MAGICAL ICE PALACE 43172 TOY CASTLE BUILDING SET (New 2019; 701 Pieces) is a reissue of the previously discontinued 41148 set of the same name that was originally released in 2017 (also at a retail price of $79.99). Some of the ad pages in the 43172 building instructions are different, but the models are the same.

The Elsa’s Magical Castle model isn’t large, but it has loads of sparkle and detail; and tons of play potential in the many accessories (e,g., castle furniture, Olaf’s train) and moving parts (e,g., swirling staircase, snow slide). It’s one of my all-time favorite LEGO buildings--one that I have on permanent display (alongside my big Disney castle model).

What I love most about Elsa’s castle is that it incorporates a lot of transparent “Frozen blue” bricks, many of which have embedded silver sparkles. I love shiny stuff, and Elsa’s shimmering cape is something to behold. I also love trains, so Olaf’s train is another plus. The little snowmen’s teeter-totter (near the snow fort) is fun. I don’t really care for the scary snow monster, but it helps in reenacting scenes from the movie.

Some of the model’s sparkle is added with stickers, but there aren’t a lot of stickers, and they’re easy to apply. There is a moving slide that opens and closes the tall castle front doors. There is a spiral staircase that swirls open when you turn a knob. The figures of Elsa and Anna are true to the cartoon figures in the Frozen film. This is truly a great, classic LEGO set, based on a great, classic Disney movie.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Disney Frozen Elsa's Magical Ice Palace 43172 Toy Castle Building Kit with Mini Dolls, Castle Playset with Popular Frozen Characters Including Elsa, Olaf, Anna and More (701 Pieces)

text_fidelity_a:
Niya - a game by Bruno Cathala I love to play games! Over the years we've played lots of party games and games for groups (may have something to do with having 6 kids), but now that we are empty nesters we have been looking for games for 2 players. We got this at a local games store and we absolutely love it!
I don't particularly like games that are super complex, where you have to read every card and figure out how it interacts with the other 200 cards. Niya can be explained in 5 minutes and played in 10-15 minutes, but it is also strategic.
The quality is excellent, with a great metal tin instead of a cardboard box, sturdy board pieces, and weighty playing pieces.
The artwork is very nice, with a clean, simple aesthetic. Very Japanese!
I have two very nit picky complaints about it. One of the categories on the board pieces is pines. They look very much like cacti to me. The other is that on the black pieces the black hair of the characters kind of disappears. I wish they had outlined them somehow.
All in all a great game. Highly recommended.
text_fidelity_b: Niya - a game by Bruno Cathala

BOMENNE Build-on Brick Mug,Funny Novelty Coffee Mug Compatible with Lego,Creative DIY Building Blocks Cup,Birthday Party Cups For Kids,Unique Gifts For Christmas,Black I should have read some of the reviews before wasting money on these mugs.

I have spent the last 90 minutes trying to decorate this mug. The parts sent with the mug do not attach; you can place them but they immediately fall off. Those parts fit to one another very well, but they decline to play nicely (or at all) with their mug.

I tried LEGO pieces and they do not want to be pressed onto the mug. I really cannot blame them.

The only block pieces that do fit onto the mug are ones I had purchased from Dollar Tree. They meld easily with the mug and hold beautifully. Unfortunately, the only surface that will accept them is the front of the mug. As you can see from the pictures they are holding well, but the rest of the mug surfaces are...well, I am trying so hard not to be all negative and everything, but the mug is so poorly designed and sloppily made that nohting will attach at all, not LEGO, not the mug company's blocks and not even the pieces of white bread that I smushed together and tried to mold to the pegs and holes. It stuck whilst still moist and them fell off when it dried and I picked up the mug to check.

We are a totally dedicated LEGO family. We have even indoctrinated...coerced...um...lovingly brought my son-in-law into the LEGO Love. We give and share those precious bricks at every gifting opportunity. There have been times when my grandchildren are out playing with their friends and my daughter and I are still inside playing. I recently learned that the one set she would love to have is the Friend's Heartlake Hotel, but by that time it was already hovering around $400.00. I am thinking that I will make provisions in my will for her to have one.

Sadly, I bought two of these. Double the heartbreak. Do not buy this unless you are planning to do what I intend to do with them. I have a tiny ton of old costume jewelry that I use for crafting and I am going to use Gorilla Glue to cover the mug with some cool bits and bobs of jewelry. That will be a totally huge and groovy improvement to the really quite pathetic red C that is now on the mug. I am an old granny and am surprised how disappointed I am with this mug.

Please protect your loved ones and buy something else. You can buy some nice real LEGO packs for the $26.00 I wasted on this crap, or a very large amount of blocks and accessories of the blocks sold at Dollar Tree. Tell them I sent you.

Love,
Granny

text_fidelity_a:
DC Superheroes Top Trumps Match Board Game This is a fun game. My boyfriend and I played it. It is only a two-player match game like tic-tac-toe or battleship. The youngest player starts and both players get two cards which they keep face down until the end of the game. The first player pushes out a cube in the top left corner of the game grid. The next player then pushes out another cube on the board with that same cube. The play continues with each player pushing out the next cube with the previous cube just played without using the same grid hole. The idea is to match five of the same characters in a row either horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. When one player indicates a match, the losing player turns over their cards and if the character on one of the cards matches the winning players match, then that person now wins the game. If there is no match, then the winner keeps his win.

The game is simple, yet fun, and is full of strategy. There are two negatives, however. The game case is difficult to open and it feels like I am going to break off the plastic prongs when I pull it apart. Also, the game wobbles a bit when the outside "wings" are down. Third, it is easy to knock all the cubes out of the game grid. As my boyfriend was playing, he titled the game just a bit to see the characters better and many of the cubes fell out. Other than the lackluster quality of the game parts, the game itself is wonderfully simple and tremendous fun.
text_fidelity_b: DC Superheroes Top Trumps Match Board Game

NEHEME NH760 Drones with 1080P HD Camera for Adults, WIFI FPV Live Video, RC Quadcopter Foldable Drones for Kids Beginners, Headless Mode, One Key Start Toys Gifts with 2 Batteries, Upgraded Version I've used a LOT of drones, from professional DJI models to the cheap pocket sized tiny drones. I love flying the little ones around the house and practicing zipping in between banisters and over bookcases, and I love flying my larger DJI Phantoms and Mavic outside for real shots of landscapes and aerial photography. I was hoping this would be a good in-between product.
It is not really.
It looks a lot like the Mavic Mini, but that immediately falls apart when you hold it and realize how cheap the construction is. That's ok, it costs about 1/3 of what I paid for my Mavic Mini. But I've held cheaper drones that felt better than this. The controls are very much like the cheaper smaller drones that have been around for years (including the flip feature, which is admittedly fun), and the quality of the camera has not improved since the first cheap one I tried 5-6 years ago. Find the most basic/free cell phone you can buy from a store shelf a few years ago and the camera quality will look better than this. That was ok back then, especially since I recall paying 40-60 dollars for those drones and the cheapest DJI was closer to 800! But now, I was expecting better. At this price tag and with 2022 tech, I was hoping it would be some sort of bridge-gap product.
The downside to being larger is that it sort of doesn't fit into either category... Unlike a more expensive drone with GPS and fine tuned motors, it does not handle itself well outdoors unless there is ZERO wind (nearly impossible, especially as you climb altitude), and it is too big to fly indoors without being in danger of hitting something and actually doing damage (unlike the smaller cheaper ones). I actually can't think of a situation that I'd like to use this with: I'd recommend a smaller camera drone to play with indoors and once you are approaching the triple digit dollar amount, I'd recommend even a used Mavic Mini for outdoor flying (much more stable with GPS, and a stabilized go-pro quality camera etc).
It does come with two batteries which is nice since they go quickly, and the carrying case is pretty nice too. I guess if you're in the market for a drone like this, it DOES work so it deserves at least 3 stars, but I'm slightly disappointed with what you get for the asking price.
text_fidelity_b: NEHEME NH760 Drones with 1080P HD Camera for Adults, WIFI FPV Live Video, RC Quadcopter Foldable Drones for Kids Beginners, Headless Mode, One Key Start Toys Gifts with 2 Batteries, Upgraded Version

text_fidelity_a:
SmartLab Toys It's Alive Slime Lab SmartLab Toys It’s Alive Slime Lab is just one of dozens and dozens of slime toys intended to fascinate the young scientist in your home. The way most of these labs works is similar: Combine the included slime mix, if any exists, with a few household items like baking soda, vinegar, cornstarch, etc., and let the fun begin.

This slime toy works like the others in terms of the mixing, but it is also different than others, and I mean that in a good way. With this slime lab, the mixture is placed atop a motor that vibrates for greater effect. Kids can watch the colors and textures swirl around as the vibrations create some fun and very visual patterns. The instructions include 20 different recipes for slime and each can be made using items found in most kitchens.

What I probably like best about this slime lab is the lack of mess! Okay, there is some mess but in relative terms, the messiness is kept under control very well. The key difference is that, with most other slime labs my kids have used, messiness is encouraged. These other labs involve sticking hands in the slime, spreading it with your hands, and so on. This is messy and gross, and if multiple kids are involved, they often end up smearing it on each other, splattering it on the floors and more. There is no problem like that with SmartLab. The slime, for the most part, stays in the bowl, out of your way.

Educational toys are nice and SmartLab Toys It’s Alive Slime Lab is a toy that does get kids thinking and asking questions. My girls like it and have returned to it more than once, creating more slime and learning about household chemicals and how they react. It’s a good choice of toy that will keep kids entertained as they learn.
text_fidelity_b: SmartLab Toys It's Alive Slime Lab

TEAM MAGNUS 18ft XL Slip and Slide - Heavy Duty Inflatable Slide with Central Sprinkler and XL Crash Pad I’ve used the slide on a slight slope and almost a flat surface. PRO’s: width and length of slide (twice as long as other slides in target audience), easy setup/operate/put away, splash zone (pool at end) works to stop toddlers. CON’s: the streaming water that “wets” the slide is too wide near the end of the slide and hardly existing at the start of the slide. The splash zone edges (inflated) nearest to the slide don’t ensure participant won’t slide over and miss splash zone.
A simple design improvement would be to have far less watering holes for the slip and slide near the splash zone and progressively more as you near the starting point. This to be is the largest flaw in the slide.
There are ways to “work around” the lack of water on the slide (the lack of slipperiness) but the product should fix this vs the customer having workarounds.

Franklin Sports Giant Wooden Dice These dice are beautifully made of solid pine. Playing games with these are fun but play responsibly. Displaying the dice as works of art is equally as great.

Provided in the package:
- Six die that weigh a combined 4.6 pounds. (See the attached pictures for an idea of size relative to two of my cats and their water fountain.)
- A strong canvas pouch for carrying the dice.
- A folded one-page pamphlet with two game variations and a sample score card for copying.

Each die is beautiful and each "number point" (i.e. dots) on the same die face is painted a rich coffee brown or dark tan. However, the "number points" are various shades of coffee brown on each side of the same die, so there is a slight inconsistency in color there. Nevertheless, this does not take away from their beauty. One should discount the "life-sized" claim. They are large but all of them stacked three high, side-by-side, do not even reach the height of a poised cat as you can see from my photos. When used for play instead of art, the round edge of each die provides for a smooth roll and reduction of injury to property or person. Although this is rated for ages 6 and above, I HIGHLY RECOMMEND children, adults, and pets stay far back when rolling the dice.

My boyfriend and I played the first game on my inside carpet since it was raining outside. I made sure to remove any items that could break around the area we were playing and I had to keep shooing the cats away. I originally thought we had to roll all six die at once (which is impossible). Therefore, when playing the two games in the instructions, roll each die one at a time because they are too large to roll together. The instructions should say that, however, because the first thought I had is "How am I going to roll these six die all at once," when the instructions said "roll the dice"?

My boyfriend loved the dice and the game even though I won. Since each die is heavy, it is extremely important to throw each die gently. I can see unsupervised children or drunk adults throwing these at each other and causing serious damage or death. As long as everyone plays responsibly, hours of fun and friendly competition are awaiting those who play this lawn or carpeted basement "game."
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Giant Wooden Dice

Prime Climb Great game for helping kids understand factors and learn their multiplication/division (and addition/subtraction) facts, plus it's FUN! The part that initially drew me in for where my kids are was the color coding of the basic primes, and by extension the use of those colors to represent factors in the products. Then, it arrived and the gameplay was really fun--there are two ten sided dice and you can add, subtract, multiply or divide the number you are on by each die in turn to move. If you land on a prime you get to draw a Prime Card, which you can either use right away or save for later to benefit yourself or target an opponent, depending on whether the card is an Action card or Keeper. The first person to move both pawns to 101 wins. If you get tired of the standard rules, though, they apparently have some variations here: [...] but I have not yet tried any--looking forward to doing so after we've played through a few more times.

Oh and keep in mind that it takes longer the more players there are--folks with younger kids might want to keep it to 2 or 3 players so it doesn't go so long, or modify the rules so people don't get sent back to start so often. text_fidelity_a:
CUSTOM SABER Smooth Swing RGBX Light Saber, Motion Control for Turn on/Off The Blade, 12 Sound Fonts Light Saber, Support Dueling, Light Saber for Adults Gift with Belt Clip and Blade Plug-Sliver [[VIDEOID:a47326bb48b328d18558c86fcccc38a1]] THE GOOD:
--------------
* Very high quality. The handle alone is 12.4 ounces.
* USB-C charging port.
* Belt clip included.
* Decorative blade plug is included. This is cool if you just want to display the handle without the blade. You can cap off your handle with this decorative plug.
* Bottom of the hilt is a decorative speaker cap instead of a pommel/coupling.
* Hilt is 1-1/4 inch. This will connect with other 1.25 inch handles to create a duo saber. Another dominant size on the market is a smaller 1 and 1/8th diameter version. This one will not thread onto 1.25 hilts, so to create duo sabers with different brands, be sure the hilts are the same size.
* All the special effects are pretty much standard: Lock up effect, changing colors, steady, pulse, unstable, etc. This version also has quotes. Watch my video to see a demo

THE BAD:
------------
* Pommel or coupling is not included. As mentioned above, bottom of the hilt is a decorative speaker cap. When you remove this speaker cap, the bottom of this hilt will be male. So to create the duo saber, your other saber should have a coupling so that it's female.
* My light saber did not charge properly out the box. When you plug it in to charge, it'll loudly announce, "Charging!" Then the red light will blink slowly. When it is complete, it will say, "READY," and the red light will be stable, no blinking. Chances are you're not going to be present when the saber says READY. But as long as you see the red light is stable and not blinking, then you'll know it's fully charged. My issue was that after 10 hrs of charging, the red light was still blinking slowly, and the saber wouldn't turn on. I contacted customer support and they had a solution ready to go. So this seems like a common problem. I talk about this at the end of my video, so watch it if you have a charging issue. My saber is charging properly now. So the word to describe this saber is, finicky.

I'll give this an overall rating of 4-Stars.
text_fidelity_b: CUSTOM SABER Smooth Swing RGBX Light Saber, Motion Control for Turn on/Off The Blade, 12 Sound Fonts Light Saber, Support Dueling, Light Saber for Adults Gift with Belt Clip and Blade Plug-Sliver

Mega Bloks HALO Dual Mode UNSC Warthog Sometimes when I get a box of Bloks, I chuck the instructions, dump them in with the rest of my collection, and make something cool with some of my favorite new pieces. I really liked the look of this one though, and I haven't followed the instructions for a while, so I actually built it to spec. I wasn't sure if there was any logic to all the separate and nested baggies, but half way through I concluded that the answer was "very little". I dumped them all in a dark colored jewelry display tray and things went much more smoothly. I definitely learned a few things about how some of the pieces can work together, and the end result came out looking nicer than most of the pre-built toys out there these days, but fully customizable. There are quite a lot of Bloks left over after completing the main instructions, and they've included some suggested modifications with build instructions, like the missile launcher in one of the pictures.

There were some minor flaws. The windshield doesn't attach very solidly. The two dudes are so burly and heavily armored that they don't fit inside gracefully. A few of the pieces shrunk just enough when they cooled that they ripple a bit differently than the things they are supposed to look smooth with. Lastly, while the instructions are very good, this set is mostly different shades of black and dark silver, which weren't adequately differentiated in the pictures which made locating the right parts in the heap difficult

The build process, with its sorting and instruction struck me as.something that would be a good project to do with my 3 year old son, since he is developing all the needed skills right now. Maybe instead of a puzzle, we'll build a warthog together on the next rainy day.
text_fidelity_b: Mega Bloks HALO Dual Mode UNSC Warthog

RoseArt Memoji Jewelry Color N Shrink Deluxe Party Pack Arts & Crafts I like craft kits like this for the kids. I like them going outside and being able to entertain themselves without having things do the entertaining for them. And I like having crafts like this where they can sit indoors and make things that they can give away as a gift, or they can use it themselves.
With this MeJoji kit, they can make 5 bracelets and necklaces. They come up with their own designs so it makes them unique to who they are.
The older kids help the younger ones trace and color a design using the included pencils. I then take the colored pieces and put them into the oven so harden them up and shrink them. Then we just added it to a ring and then slipped a cord through. To hold the memoji into place, we knotted the cord around it so it stayed in one place and didn't slide around.
I did have some beads, from some other kit we had, and added those to the cord. Just something to fill in the space and to add a lot more color.
Some do come with the kit but, we liked adding more.
My box was also opened prior to us getting it. The piece of tape that is suppose to be holding it closed was peeled open and it was nasty dirty.
Only has 3 design sheets in it. A bit of a bummer. Reading how many others got opened kits, I wouldn't ever buy another kit. Wouldn't spend money on things that are opened and items missing out of it. And a big waste of time having to contact the company and returning it.

text_fidelity_a: Pass the Stache Board Game Watching a group of 13 year olds play Moustache Smash is like watching a Black Friday sale with everyone fighting for the same discounted towels. I couldn't help but laugh hysterically as each girl held the mustache up to her face then frantically tried to be the first to smash the card that either matched the color or the shape of their mustache. (Mind you they had to remember which mustache they chose and what it looked like because they have to keep it up on their face at all times when the game is in play - until it's time to snatch a card). The game comes with 6 mustaches on very solid plastic sticks. There is a suction cup at the end of the mustache that allows the playing card to be snatched up quite easily. It's best to play on a solid surface to make sure the card stays put. There are 32 mustache cards of various colors and shapes. Each player takes a turn being the dealer. The dealer flips the card over for all to see - but can't cheat by flipping the card facing them first. IF a player accidentally snatches up the wrong mustache, they have to return it plus two more mustaches (if they have them) from their stash. It goes into a pot for the next player who correctly snatches up a mustache to claim. When all 32 cards are dealt, the game is over. The player left standing with the most 'stashes wins. The cards are in perfect squares - keeping the field even for all players. The mustaches feel rubbery so are less likely to cause harm if accidentally smacked into another players hand. The one thing I suggest is you have the camera at the ready! I have some great video and excellent pictures that I was able to share with the players' parents. Unfortunately, without the parents' permissions, I cannot display any of the videos or photos. They weren't comfortable with their children being seen. The recommended age is 7 and up, but I can easily see a 5 year old handling this well. I would also be willing to play with a group of adults. For $15.99 with free prime shipping, it is a great birthday or Christmas gift without breaking the budget. Plus, there are no tiny pieces to lose or step on. (BONUS!)  Keep in mind, though, that there are only 6 mustaches... so a max of 6 players can play at one time.
text_fidelity_b: Pass the Stache Board Game

text_fidelity_a:
Alex Art Wooden Dough Tools Set Kids Art and Craft Activity What you see is what you get! This fun set of clay manipulation tools would make a perfect gift alongside either play doh or one of the more sophisticated and fluffier types of modeling clay such as[[ASIN:B011TRQ3TO Sago Brothers 36 Colors Ultra Light Modeling Magic Air Dry Clay Crafts Kit]].

I think my favorites are the three rolling wheels, which are suited to small hands and fun to use. The wood has a light coating of some manner of varnish or slightly slick treatment, so it doesn't stick to the clay too badly, and keeps things fun to use. I like the bright primary colors in the natural wood tone, and the diverse shapes are a lot of fun. The only thing you should know is that a few of these are not entirely safe for extremely active toddlers, so this is a toy that you will supervise and make sure that nobody is sprinting down the hall with a small pointed spear. When used as directed and not as a weapon (mothers of small boys will understand my caveat), this is such a fun set!

I actually held one of them back, the rolling wheel that has little squares stamped into it, so my son can help me make peanut butter cookies by gently pushing the cookie with his roller. This one will remain food safe only, and the rest will be played with with modeling clays and play dough. I don't think these would be as fun and successful with more grown-up clays such as Fimo just because the surface area is so large and usually you are creating giant rough sculptures with an expensive material like Fimo or Sculpey. This is definitely the sort of thing you would use with children's modeling clay. A great starter set that would make a great auxiliary to a simple modeling dough gift.
text_fidelity_b: Alex Art Wooden Dough Tools Set Kids Art and Craft Activity

I sat it in the middle of my concrete driveway and hit the take off button and it took off. I got the nerve to change the flight parameters in the settings. I changed it to the max height and distance. I didn’t record a video in this mode but I took it up 300 feet and to a distance of 4000 feet from the controller. I could barely see it. Got very scared and thought I might lose it so I hit the home button. Within 10 seconds she was back in clear view. The views are amazing. I didn’t know there were so many interesting things around my house. I can’t wait to take it to my office and take some videos of my dealership. After this flight, I can say I’d definitely buy it again. I’ve never had so much fun without leaving my driveway. So again, get you one. Thanks Deerc.

text_fidelity_a: Barbie Fashionistas Doll 112 I am a long time Barbie fan. I loved playing with them when I was young, in the 70's. Then in the 90's I collected them. Then in the 2000's I bought them for my little girl. She's graduating from high school next month, but I still love Barbie! I got these for my 5 year old niece to play with when she visits us. I love the variety of body types in this set. I think that's one of the best changes to happen to Barbie ever! This set has 4 different dolls. There's the traditional Barbie that we all love. Then there's the curvy African American doll, a short, petite doll that looks like she could be Hispanic, and a tall , dark hair doll. The thing I love about them (their differences) is also slightly problematic. They all wear different size clothes/shoes. While, that's pretty normal in the real world, it's more difficult in the Barbie world. Some of the dolls could probably get away with sharing clothes, but curvy doll is out of luck. I hope to see more curvy doll size clothes in the future! And if you are planning to gift this, be aware that they don't come in the typical pink Barbie box.
